data.narrative:
Mytra is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Walti and Ahmad Baitalmal that has raised $200M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine private robotics companies at Series B through Series D stages, including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), alongside one public comparator.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $200M raised as a proxy for current value, applied a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $340M. Peer-median analysis across the seven robotics-sector comparables at matching or adjacent stages produced a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. These methods produced a wide spread reflecting stage and capital structure heterogeneity within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $289M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $995M. The substantial variance between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects uncertainty around whether Mytra's capital-raise profile and maturity align with the lower (Series B) or upper (Series D) end of the comparable range. Resolution requires clarity on revenue traction, customer concentration, and technical differentiation relative to peers.
